title: AI in Excel 3: Claude in Excel

questions.question: For which job does the course point you to Claude in Excel rather than Copilot?

answerOptions.text: Running a forecast with Python in Excel
answerOptions.rationale: Python advanced analysis is a Copilot feature.

answerOptions.text: Reviewing a plan in Copilot's Plan mode
answerOptions.rationale: Plan mode belongs to Copilot.

answerOptions.text: Asking Analyze Data for a suggested chart
answerOptions.rationale: Analyze Data is Excel's own built-in tool.

answerOptions.text: Explaining a multi-sheet workbook you inherited, with cell citations
answerOptions.rationale: Claude is strong at whole-workbook reasoning and explaining with citations.

questions.question: Which Claude plan do you need to sign in to Claude in Excel?

answerOptions.text: A paid plan: Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise
answerOptions.rationale: The add-in needs a paid Claude plan; the free plan will not sign in.

answerOptions.text: The free Claude plan is enough
answerOptions.rationale: The free plan will not sign in to the add-in.

answerOptions.text: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
answerOptions.rationale: That licence is for Copilot, not for Claude.

answerOptions.text: No plan; the add-in signs in with your Microsoft account only
answerOptions.rationale: You sign in with your own Claude account on a paid plan.

questions.question: On a Mac, which shortcut opens or closes the Claude in Excel pane?

answerOptions.text: Command + Option + C
answerOptions.rationale: That is not the shortcut taught for Claude.

answerOptions.text: Control + `
answerOptions.rationale: Control and backtick shows formulas.

answerOptions.text: Control + Option + C
answerOptions.rationale: Control Option C toggles the Claude pane on Excel for Mac.

answerOptions.text: Command + T
answerOptions.rationale: Command T creates a Table.

questions.question: You search for Claude in Microsoft Marketplace. What should you check before clicking Add?

answerOptions.text: That it has the most downloads in the store
answerOptions.rationale: Popularity does not confirm who published it.

answerOptions.text: That the publisher is Anthropic, because copycat add-ins exist
answerOptions.rationale: You are giving the add-in access to your data, so check who made it.

answerOptions.text: That AutoSave is switched off
answerOptions.rationale: AutoSave has nothing to do with installing add-ins.

answerOptions.text: That your file has no formulas in it
answerOptions.rationale: Claude reads formulas; they do not block installation.

questions.question: Claude has listed four problems in an inherited P&L. Why does the lesson approve one fix per message instead of saying "fix everything"?

answerOptions.text: Claude can only make one change per day
answerOptions.rationale: There is no such limit; the reason is easier checking.

answerOptions.text: Fixing everything at once deletes the original file
answerOptions.rationale: It does not delete the file; it just makes the changes hard to review.

answerOptions.text: One fix per message makes Claude cheaper to use
answerOptions.rationale: The lesson's reason is review and undo, not cost.

answerOptions.text: Each change is easy to check, and Command Z can undo any single step
answerOptions.rationale: Several changes at once are hard to review.

questions.question: What is the safe way to clean a messy customer list with Claude?

answerOptions.text: Clean into a new sheet, keep the original untouched and add a Changes column
answerOptions.rationale: You can compare line by line and audit every change.

answerOptions.text: Let Claude overwrite the original so there is only one version
answerOptions.rationale: Never overwrite your only copy when cleaning with AI.

answerOptions.text: Clean it, then delete the Changes column to save space
answerOptions.rationale: The Changes column is your audit trail.

answerOptions.text: Skip the row count check if the result looks tidy
answerOptions.rationale: A row count shows whether any row was dropped.

questions.question: After Claude extracts a bank statement from a PDF into Excel, how do you prove nothing was missed?

answerOptions.text: Ask Claude whether it extracted everything
answerOptions.rationale: Its own answer is not proof; the PDF totals are.

answerOptions.text: Check that the sheet has no #REF! errors
answerOptions.rationale: A dropped transaction shows no error.

answerOptions.text: Reconcile total debits, total credits, closing balance and row count with the PDF's summary box
answerOptions.rationale: Any difference means a missing or doubled line.

answerOptions.text: Sort the table by date
answerOptions.rationale: Sorting does not show whether a line is missing.

questions.question: You open a file from an unknown supplier and ask Claude to work on it. What is the main risk the course warns about?

answerOptions.text: The file will turn off AutoSave
answerOptions.rationale: That is not the risk the course describes.

answerOptions.text: Prompt injection: the file can hide instructions in its text, so read Claude's plan before approving
answerOptions.rationale: Treat file content as data and check what Claude plans to do.

answerOptions.text: Claude will refuse to read any file not made in Excel for Mac
answerOptions.rationale: Claude reads the workbook regardless of where it was made.

answerOptions.text: The file will cancel your Claude plan
answerOptions.rationale: Files cannot change your plan; the risk is hidden instructions.
